why: The floors of the Edificio Central registered against the building as Brian measured it with a tape (docs/map/survey), not as the cadastre draws it. ec-register.json laid the plans on the cadastre, whose north wing reaches the Calle 63 curb and whose lot runs to the Carrera 9A: the survey found the wall 6 m back from that curb and the building 3 m shorter behind. Against the measured walls the evacuation plans turn out to be in proportion: once the Calle 63 wall is where it is, the north wing's inner wall and the end of the north connection fall within 0.3 m of where the tape puts them. Each pair is one wall: where the plan puts the rooms against it, then where the rooms go, a wall's thickness (10 units, 0.3 m) inside the measured face.
x why: The Calle 63 wall of the ground floor (survey 56-62: 5.95 to 6.64 m from the curb; the second floor's rooms start 42 units before it on their plan, the 1.2 m the wing is carried out over the street). The north wing's inner wall, 5.39 m along the Carrera 9 Bis from the corner. The end of the north connection, 6.22 m further. The tower's east face, which did not move.
fit why: Until the architectural plans arrive, the drawings follow the building: every room a wall (0.3 m) inside the floor's margin - the building's parts on that floor, as surveyed - and clear of the stairs and lifts that climb it.
keep slanted why: Brian: the auditorium keeps the shape its own plan draws, and it stands slanted, along the Carrera 9 Bis; so do the rooms he outlined in it until P1's "turned" block draws them. Every other room is square, as the building is.

central lifts.why: As ec-register.json stacks them on every floor: the tower did not move.

main stair.why: Beside the central lifts and as deep as they are, as these two floors' plans draw it, which leaves the corridor that runs under both; where Brian set it in the floor editor. ec-register.json stacks it 2.8 m deeper from P3 up, as those plans draw it, until they are registered against the survey too.

lifts by the toilets.why: As ec-register.json stacks them from P2 up.

emergency stair.why: As ec-register.json stacks it from P2 up.

north stair.why: Where P1's plan puts it once the plan is on the measured walls: at the front of the north wing on the Carrera 9 Bis, as wide as the wing's ground floor (5.39 m), a wall inside it. P3 to P5 still stack it where the cadastre had the wing, until they are registered against the survey too.

P1.y why: The plan's first row of rooms goes a wall inside the tower's front on the Carrera 9 Bis, and its last a wall inside the back wall, 5.48 m from the Carrera 9A curb (survey 53). The plan's depth between the two, 1643 units, is the measured one, 1638: the plan was only laid 3 m too far back, onto the cadastre's lot line.

drop.P1-15: Open floor north of the Cafetería No. 1 in Brian's sketch of 2026-10-21, between the shop and the lifts by the bathrooms; no room.
drop.P1-16: The food court the plan's tracing drew; in Brian's sketch of 2026-10-21 it is part of the Cafetería No. 1.
drop.P1-22: The plan's box beside the treasury is the Tienda in Brian's sketch of 2026-10-21 (P1-TIENDA).
drop.P1-24: The plan's long block east of the food court; in Brian's sketch of 2026-10-21 it is part of the Cafetería No. 1.
drop.P1-25: The plan's strip along the Calle 63 is the Cafetería No. 2 in Brian's sketch of 2026-10-21 (P1-CAFETERIA-NO-2).
drop.P1-33: In Brian's sketch of 2026-10-21 this corner is part of the Cocina and of the box by the ramp.
drop.P1-34: In Brian's sketch of 2026-10-21 this box is the south end of the Cocina (P1-COCINA).
drop.P1-CAFETERIA-NO-2: Brian, 2026-10-21: the food court is one cafeteria, P1-CAFETERIA, and its north extension P1-CAFETERIA-NORTE; no second cafeteria.
drop.P1-ZONA-ESPARCIMIENT: The sanitary route plan's name for the food court's hall, which is the cafeteria: an alias of P1-CAFETERIA now.

yield.P1-17: A small box Brian drew between the north lift and the wall; squared on its own its outline folds, so it is refitted to the room it has.
yield.P1-RECEPCION: Sketched round the box beside it (P1-13); the box keeps its wall.
yield.P1-RAMPA-VEHICULAR: The emergency stair beside it keeps its wall.
yield.P1-CAFETERIA: Brian outlined the cafeteria round the rooms it reaches - the treasury, the shop, the boxes by the lifts; they keep their walls and it takes the floor between them.

outside.P1-PATIO: Brian, 2026-10-21: an open patio beside the building, between the ramp and the gate on the Carrera 9A, not under its roof. It keeps the shape he sketched; the floor's surveyed margin stays as measured.

groups.why: Everything Brian outlined on the auditorium's plan moves as one sheet onto four of its corners where the tape puts them, a wall inside: the ticket office's corner at the end of the public entrance (survey 15, 25), the angle where the slanted wall meets the blue wall (survey 26, 74), the far end of the front at the neighbour's building (survey 24, 65, 66), and the far end of the back, taken from the blue wall's length without stretching the plan. That only brings his rooms near their place while the rest of the floor is fitted, as before; "turned" draws them.

drawn.why: Brian, 2026-11-05 (#218): the hall is not square, it follows the plan. Each room is the one he outlined over the auditorium's plan (traced/ec-p1-auditorio.json), laid on the floor by the similarity that takes the plan onto the four surveyed corners above (scale and turn alone, so its walls keep their angles; 0.1 to 0.3 m off them), not by the four-corner warp. The plan's seats, its grey rows, are read off the photo the same way, and the hall keeps every one of them inside, 1.5 units clear of its walls (checked pixel by pixel: none outside). Walls two rooms share are simplified once, to 6 units, and every room is in whole units. scripts/plan-tracing/wip/aud_walls.py makes them.

spaces.why: The seats: Brian's outline of the hall, cut on the plan's east wall (fitted), and every seat the plan prints inside it with 1.5 units to spare; less the rooms round it.
The stage, as Brian outlined it.
Squared to the building, as both plans draw it, and off the lobby.
Squared to the building, as both plans draw it; between it and the lobby is the thick wall Brian described.
What is left between the hall, the stair, the prop room and the front, to the door on the front's step (survey 65-67).
Squared to the building, along the Calle 62 wall, as both plans draw it.
Brian's corners: its top along the plan's wall from the hall's east wall to the stair, its back the wing's.

spaces.name: Patio cubierto
spaces.why: Brian: behind the auditorium, between it and the Casa de Francisco de Paula Velez, a patio with a sliding roof and tables runs from the tower to the neighbours' building. One floor. From a wall behind the wing to a wall inside the lot line with the casa, which it follows.

P1.outline why: Brian (#218): the way out to the Carrera 9A is part of the Edificio Central, as wide as the plans show it, with the wall it shares with the Casa de Francisco de Paula Velez. The outline is the building's surveyed parts that reach this floor, the open patio by the ramp, and that passage: from the lobby's back wall, between the tower's east face and the casa's lot line, past the gate beside the booth to the Carrera 9A sidewalk. The plan of the floor draws the passage down to the street between the tower and a line that meets the patio behind the auditorium; that line is the casa's lot line, which the city's map puts 7 m from the tower.

corridors.name: Pasillo transversal
corridors.why: The PE's route from the exit on the Calle 63, under the north stair and the central lifts and stairs, to the door of the auditorium's lobby.

corridors.name: Paso a la salida de la Carrera 9A
corridors.why: The PE's route from the lobby's back door down the open passage beside the Casa de Francisco de Paula Velez, drawn where the survey found the way out: round the central wing's one-floor piece and through the gate between the booth at its corner and the casa's wall (survey 69-71), out to the Carrera 9A sidewalk, where the outline ends.

P1.corridors why: Only where the floor is open: the hall across the tower and the passage to the Carrera 9A. The PE's other two green routes, down the food court and across the central hall, run through the cafeteria, which Brian made one room (2026-10-21): a line there is drawn over a room, so they are not corridors.

add.why: Brian: the lobby is the south connection's whole ground floor. The auditorium's plan does not draw it; he sketched it above the plan with its four doors: to the central wing, the public entrance on the Carrera 9 Bis (survey 15, 6.30 m of front), one at the back and the one through the thick wall to the north anteroom, beside the ticket office. A wall inside the connection, as surveyed; where on each wall a door stands is as he sketched it, not measured.

P2.y why: This plan was laid in the frame higher than P1's: its first row goes a wall inside the tower's front, and the long room at the back of the tower a wall inside the back wall. Its depth comes out 5% smaller, the same 5% the plans' widths do.

groups.why: The gallery Brian marked on the first floor's plan - the seats repeated on the second floor, which he said run on over the audiovisual booth - on the same four corners as the hall below.

limits.why: Brian: the reception rises through P1 and P2. P2 has no room over it, the tower's front; the box keeps the north connection's part, which ends 6.22 m from the north wing.
The tower's east half is its seven-floor part, which ends 6 m short of the back wall; past it P1 has the one-floor piece by the exit, and P2 nothing.

It reaches from the north connection a hand into the north wing, and the connection's back wall stands 2.1 m behind the wing's, behind its planters, as Brian set it: the room ends with the connection.

drop.P2-16: The plan paints the auditorium's whole silhouette on the second floor. Brian: the hall rises through both floors, and only the gallery of seats along the Carrera 9 Bis is up here; that is drawn instead.

regular.why: Brian, 2026-11-04: the map is for the portal and both apps, so every space is rectilinear and still fits the building. Shapes follow his pencil lines, regularized: walls level or plumb, and in the auditorium's wing, which stands askew on the Carrera 9 Bis, plumb or along its two facades as the survey measures them; steps under 0.9 m go; two walls under 0.25 m apart that run side by side become one. The stairs and lifts that climb the building do not move.
